question.text: GDP measured by aggregating the output of agriculture, industry, and services sectors uses which method?

explanation.text: The Logic: The Product Method measures GDP as an aggregated flow of goods and services from the agriculture, industry and services sectors, and computes total output on a sector-wise basis. The Trap: The Income Method sums incomes such as wages, profits, rent and interest, while the Expenditure Method sums consumption, investment, government spending and net exports. Neither is described as a sector-wise aggregation of output. Note: The Product Method definition and the sector-wise aggregation of agriculture, industry and services output are covered on pages 92-93 of the NISM-Series-XV Research Analyst Certification Examination workbook (February 2026).
